## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Nandakapetavatthu* (Pv 38, also cited as 4.3) is a verse narrative within the *Petavatthu* collection of the Pali canon [Norman 1983; SuttaCentral]. In this text, a ghost gives counsel to a king concerning the severe hazards of wrong views and urges him to take refuge in the Triple Gem [SuttaCentral]. Based on internal chronological clues, K. R. Norman highlights that the poem refers to Pingalaka, a king of Surattha, who is explained by the commentator Dhammapāla as having reigned contemporary with the Mauryan emperor Dhammāsoka two centuries after the Buddha's death [Norman 1983]. Consequently, the composition of the *Nandakapetavatthu* represents a relatively late layer within the Pali canon, matching the timeline assigned to certain late verses in the *Theragāthā* and *Therīgāthā* [Norman 1983].

SuttaCentral notes curated passage-level parallels between this text and the *Khallāṭiyapetivatthu* (Pv 10), *Dhanapālaseṭṭhipetavatthu* (Pv 19), and *Tatiyanāgavimānavatthu* (Vv 62), alongside thematic and textual connections in the *Majjhima Nikāya* (MN 129, MN 130), *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 3.36), *Kathāvatthu*, and multiple Jātaka narratives [SuttaCentral]. Confirming several of these connections, DharmaNexus detects verbatim text reuse between segments of Pv 38 and Pv 19 (§36.1–38.4) as well as Pv 10 (§36.1–38.4), in addition to shared stanzas in the *Maṭṭhakuṇḍalīpetavatthu* (Pv 17), *Maṭṭhakuṇḍalīvimānavatthu* (Vv 83), *Ambasakkarapetavatthu* (Pv 36), *Serīsakapetavatthu* (Pv 37), *Serīsakavimānavatthu* (Vv 84), and *Mahānāradakassapajātaka* (Ja 545) [DharmaNexus]. Outside of canonical verse texts, DharmaNexus records substantial reuse in the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* and *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, as well as machine-aligned correspondences in Sanskrit and Tibetan texts such as the *Mahāvyutpatti*, *Lokaprajñapti*, *Karmaprajñapti*, and *Abhidharmakośabhāṣya* [DharmaNexus].
